title: حِكَايَةُ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 905–909 (Night 219, continuing nights-218; the last night of volume 1), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 219 continues the tale of Qamar al-Zamān. Al-Amjad reads Ḥayāt al-Nufūs's letter, kills the eunuch who brought it and reproaches his own mother; next day al-Asʿad sits in judgement, and Budūr in her turn sends him a love-letter in rhymed prose and verse wrapped in her braided hair, by an old woman whom he kills. The brothers tell each other what has happened and agree to keep it from their father. But when the king returns from the hunt his two wives, sick with fear, turn the matter round and accuse the princes of having forced them; and morning overtakes Shahrazād. This is the last night of the first volume of the Calcutta edition. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةَ عَشَرَ بَعْدَ الْمِائَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿata ʿashara baʿda al-miʾatayni
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the nineteenth after the two-hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the two hundred and nineteenth night,
sentences.n: al-tāsiʿata ʿashara, “nineteenth”: as in the nights before, the print has the masculine عشر where Classical Arabic would make it feminine (ʿashrata) to agree with the night; it is vocalised as printed. The ئ of المائتين is printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّهَا أَعْطَتْ وَرَقَةَ الْمُرَاسَلَةِ لِلْخَادِمِ وَأَمَرَتْهُ أَنْ يُوصِلَهَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ الْأَمْجَدِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu annahā aʿṭat waraqata al-murāsalati li-al-khādimi wa-amarathu an yūṣilahā ilā al-maliki al-Amjadi
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O fortunate king, that-she gave (the) sheet (of) the-correspondence to-the-servant, and-ordered-him that he-convey-it to the-king al-Amjad.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs gave the letter to the eunuch and ordered him to carry it to King al-Amjad.
sentences.n: Shahrazād picks up where the night before broke off; “she” in annahā is Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, al-Amjad's stepmother. waraqat al-murāsala, “the sheet of the correspondence”: murāsala, Form III verbal noun of r-s-l, “exchanging letters”, and so the letter itself. aʿṭat … li-al-khādimi: again li- marks the one who receives, where Classical would give aʿṭā two objects. awṣala, Form IV, “to convey, deliver”; -hā, “it”, is the letter.

sentences.t: فَسَارَ ذٰلِكَ الْخَادِمُ وَهُوَ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَا خَفِيَ لَهُ فِى الْغَيْبِ وَعَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ يُدَبِّرُ الْأُمُورَ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ
sentences.tr: fa-sāra dhālika al-khādimu wa-huwa lā yaʿlamu mā khafiya lahu fī al-ghaybi wa-ʿallāmu al-ghuyūbi yudabbiru al-umūra kayfa yashāʾu
sentences.l: And-went that servant, and-he not knowing what was-hidden for-him in the-unseen; and-(the)-Great-Knower (of) the-hidden-things arranges the-matters how He-wills.
sentences.i: So the eunuch went on his way, not knowing what lay hidden in store for him in the unseen; and He who knows all hidden things orders affairs as He wills.
sentences.n: wa-huwa lā yaʿlamu, “and he not knowing”: a circumstantial clause with wa-, describing the servant as he goes. mā khafiya lahu, “what was hidden for him”: lahu, “for him”, what was in store for him. The print spells fī with ى here, فى. ʿallām al-ghuyūb, “the Knower of hidden things”, is a Qurʾānic name of God (Q 5:109, 9:78); ʿallām is an intensive pattern, “the one who knows thoroughly”, and ghuyūb is the plural of ghayb, “the unseen”. The shaddas of علّام and يدبّر are printed. yudabbiru, Form II of d-b-r, “to arrange, direct”. kayfa yashāʾu, “how He wills”: kayfa introducing a clause, “however, as”. The narrator's aside warns that the servant is going to his death.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْخَادِمُ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ الْأَمْجَدِ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَنَاوَلَهُ الْمِنْدِيلَ وَبَلَّغَهُ الرِّسَالَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-khādimu ʿalā al-maliki al-Amjadi qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-nāwalahu al-mindīla wa-ballaghahu al-risālata
sentences.l: And-when entered the-servant upon the-king al-Amjad, he-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands, and-handed-him the-kerchief, and-delivered-to-him the-message.
sentences.i: When the eunuch came in to King al-Amjad, he kissed the ground before him, handed him the kerchief and delivered the message.
sentences.n: dakhala ʿalā, “to enter upon”, to come into someone's presence. qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi, “he kissed the ground between his hands”, the courtly obeisance before a king. The shaddas of قبّل and بلّغه are printed. nāwala, Form III, “to hand”, takes the person and the thing as two objects. ballagha, Form II, “to make reach, deliver”, likewise: ballaghahu al-risālata, “he delivered to him the message”.

sentences.t: فَتَنَاوَلَ الْمَلِكُ الْأَمْجَدُ الْمِنْدِيلَ مِنَ الْخَادِمِ وَفَتَحَهُ فَرَأَى الْوَرَقَةَ فَفَتَحَهَا وَقَرَأَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-tanāwala al-maliku al-Amjadu al-mindīla mina al-khādimi wa-fataḥahu fa-raʾā al-waraqata fa-fataḥahā wa-qaraʾahā
sentences.l: And-took the-king al-Amjad the-kerchief from the-servant, and-opened-it, and-saw the-sheet, and-opened-it and-read-it.
sentences.i: King al-Amjad took the kerchief from the eunuch and opened it, and he saw the letter, unfolded it and read it.
sentences.n: tanāwala, Form VI of n-w-l, “to take (what is handed)”, the counterpart of nāwala, “to hand”, in the sentence before. The ء of رأى and قرأها is printed. Each step follows the last with fa-, “and then”: the letter is inside the kerchief, so he opens one and then the other.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَهِمَ مَعْنَاهَا عَلِمَ أَنَّ امْرَأَةَ أَبِيهِ فِي عَيْنِهَا الْخِيَانَةُ وَقَدْ خَانَتْ أَبَاهُ الْمَلِكَ قَمَرَ الزَّمَانِ فِي نَفْسِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā fahima maʿnāhā ʿalima anna imraʾata abīhi fī ʿaynihā al-khiyānatu wa-qad khānat abāhu al-malika Qamara al-Zamāni fī nafsihā
sentences.l: And-when he-understood its-meaning, he-knew that (the) wife (of) his-father, in her-eye (is) the-treachery, and-indeed she-had-betrayed his-father the-king Qamar al-Zamān in her-self.
sentences.i: And when he understood what it meant, he knew that his father's wife had treachery in her eye, and that in her heart she had already betrayed his father, King Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.n: maʿnāhā, “its meaning”: -hā is the letter (al-waraqa). imraʾat abīhi, “the wife of his father”: imraʾa, “woman”, means “wife” when it is someone's; the ء of امرأة is printed. After anna the order is predicate first: fī ʿaynihā al-khiyānatu, “in her eye is the treachery”, she has betrayal in view. khāna, “to betray”, hollow verb of kh-w-n; khiyāna, its verbal noun. fī nafsihā, “in herself”: in intention, in her heart, since nothing has yet been done. abāhu is accusative, the object of khānat; abīhi before it is genitive after imraʾa.

sentences.t: فَغَضِبَ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا وَذَمَّ النِّسَاءَ عَلَى فِعْلِهِنَّ وَقَالَ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ النِّسَاءَ الْخَائِنَاتِ النَّاقِصَاتِ عَقْلًا وَدِينًا
sentences.tr: fa-ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan wa-dhamma al-nisāʾa ʿalā fiʿlihinna wa-qāla laʿana Allāhu al-nisāʾa al-khāʾināti al-nāqiṣāti ʿaqlan wa-dīnan
sentences.l: And-he-was-angry an-anger severe, and-blamed the-women for their-doing, and-said: (May) God curse the-women, the-treacherous, the-deficient in-mind and-religion!
sentences.i: He fell into a violent rage and railed against women for what they do, and said: God curse women, faithless as they are, wanting in sense and in faith!
sentences.n: ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan, “he was angry an anger severe”: the verb's own verbal noun as object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), with an adjective, intensifies it, “he was violently angry”. dhamma ʿalā, “to blame for”: ʿalā marks what is blamed; the shadda of ذمّ is printed. laʿana Allāhu, “God cursed”: a perfect used as a curse, “may God curse”. The ئ of الخائنات is printed. al-nāqiṣāt ʿaqlan wa-dīnan, “deficient in mind and religion”: ʿaqlan and dīnan are accusatives of specification (tamyīz), saying in what respect they fall short; the phrase echoes a well-known ḥadīth about women, and al-Amjad turns it on the whole sex.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ جَرَّدَ سَيْفَهُ وَقَالَ لِلْخَادِمِ وَيْلَكَ يَا عَبْدَ السُّوءِ أَتَحْمِلُ الْمُرَاسَلَةَ الْمُشْتَمِلَةَ عَلَى الْخِيَانَةِ مِنْ زَوْجَةِ سَيِّدِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu jarrada sayfahu wa-qāla li-al-khādimi waylaka yā ʿabda al-sūʾi a-taḥmilu al-murāsalata al-mushtamilata ʿalā al-khiyānati min zawjati sayyidika
sentences.l: Then he drew his-sword and-said to-the-servant: Woe-to-you, O slave (of) the-evil! Do-you-carry the-letter, the-containing (of) the-treachery, from (the) wife (of) your-master?
sentences.i: Then he drew his sword and said to the eunuch: Damn you, you wicked slave! Do you carry a letter full of treachery from your master's wife?
sentences.n: thumma innahu, “then (it is that) he”: the narrator's usual way of moving on. jarrada, Form II, “to bare, unsheathe”; its shadda is printed. waylaka, “woe to you”: wayl with the suffix, an accusative of exclamation. ʿabd al-sūʾ, “slave of evil”, a bad slave: the iḍāfa does the work of an adjective. The print itself points أَتَحمل, the question a- and the fatḥa of ta-; the rest is ours. mushtamila ʿalā, Form VIII participle of sh-m-l, “containing, comprising”. zawjat sayyidika, “your master's wife”: the eunuch's master is the king, Qamar al-Zamān, so the letter he carries is treachery against his own master.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَا خَيْرَ فِيكَ يَا أَسْوَدَ اللَّوْنِ وَالصَّحِيفَةِ يَا قَبِيحَ الْمَنْظَرِ وَالطَّبِيعَةِ السَّخِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi innahu lā khayra fīka yā aswada al-lawni wa-al-ṣaḥīfati yā qabīḥa al-manẓari wa-al-ṭabīʿati al-sakhīfati
sentences.l: And-by-God, indeed-it-is (that) no good (is) in-you, O black (of) the-colour and-the-record, O ugly (of) the-look and-the-nature, the-feeble!
sentences.i: By God, there is no good in you, you creature black of skin and black of record, ugly to look at and base by nature!
sentences.n: wa-Allāhi, “by God”: wa- of oaths, taking the genitive. innahu lā khayra fīka: innahu, “indeed it (is that)”, introduces the whole clause; lā khayra, “no good at all”, lā of total denial with an accusative noun without tanwīn. aswad al-lawn wa-al-ṣaḥīfa, “black of colour and of record”: an adjective governing nouns in an iḍāfa, “black as to colour”. The ṣaḥīfa is the record of a person's deeds, kept for the Day of Judgement; a “black record” is a sinful one. The insult plays on the eunuch's colour, as such abuse of black slaves often does in the Nights. qabīḥ al-manẓar, “ugly of aspect”. sakhīf, “flimsy, feeble, base”, agrees with al-ṭabīʿa. The last words fall into rhyme: al-ṣaḥīfa / al-sakhīfa.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ ضَرَبَهُ بِالسَّيْفِ فِي عُنُقِهِ فَعَزَلَ رَأْسَهُ عَنْ جُثَّتِهِ وَطَوَى الْمِنْدِيلَ عَلَى مَا فِيهِ وَوَضَعَهُ فِي جَيْبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ḍarabahu bi-al-sayfi fī ʿunuqihi fa-ʿazala raʾsahu ʿan juththatihi wa-ṭawā al-mindīla ʿalā mā fīhi wa-waḍaʿahu fī jaybihi
sentences.l: Then he-struck-him with-the-sword on his-neck, and-separated his-head from his-body; and-folded the-kerchief upon what (was) in-it, and-put-it in his-pocket.
sentences.i: Then he struck him on the neck with the sword and parted his head from his body; and he folded the kerchief over what was in it and put it away in the breast of his robe.
sentences.n: bi-al-sayfi: bi- of the instrument, “with the sword”. fī ʿunuqihi, “in his neck”: fī where English says “on”. ʿazala, “to set apart, remove”, here of a head struck off. The ء of رأسه and the shadda of جثّته are printed. juththa, “body”, often a corpse. ṭawā … ʿalā mā fīhi, “folded … over what was in it”: the letter and the braids. jayb is the opening at the breast of a robe, used as a pocket.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ عَلَى أُمِّهِ وَأَعْلَمَهَا بِمَاجَرَى وَسَبَّهَا وَشَتَمَهَا وَقَالَ كُلُّكُنَّ أَنْحَسُ مِنْ بَعْضِكُنَّ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala ʿalā ummihi wa-aʿlamahā bi-mā jarā wa-sabbahā wa-shatamahā wa-qāla kullukunna anḥasu min baʿḍikunna
sentences.l: Then he-went-in upon his-mother, and-informed-her of-what-happened, and-reviled-her and-abused-her, and-said: All-of-you (women) (are) more-ill-omened than one-another.
sentences.i: Then he went in to his mother, told her what had happened, and cursed and abused her, saying: Each of you women is viler than the next!
sentences.n: His mother is Queen Budūr; she has done nothing, but he turns on her as a woman. aʿlama, Form IV, “to inform”, takes bi- for the thing one is told: aʿlamahā bi-mā jarā, “informed her of what had happened”. The print runs bi-mā jarā together as بماجرى; it is kept as set. The shaddas of امّه, سبّها, كلكنّ and بعضكنّ are printed. sabba and shatama, “to revile” and “to abuse”, a near-synonym pair. -kunna, “you”, feminine plural: he speaks to his mother as one of all women. anḥasu min baʿḍikunna, “more ill-omened than one another”: anḥas, elative of naḥs, “ill luck, baleful”; the phrase says that each is worse than the rest, all equally bad.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ لَوْلَا أَنِّي أَخَافُ إِسَاءَةَ الْأَدَبِ فِي حَقِّ وَالِدِي قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ وَأَخِي الْمَلِكِ الْأَسْعَدِ لَأَدْخُلَنَّ عَلَيْهَا وَأَضْرِبَنَّ عُنُقَهَا كَمَا ضَرَبْتُ عُنُقَ خَادِمِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi al-ʿaẓīmi lawlā annī akhāfu isāʾata al-adabi fī ḥaqqi wālidī Qamari al-Zamāni wa-akhī al-maliki al-Asʿadi la-adkhulanna ʿalayhā wa-aḍribanna ʿunuqahā kamā ḍarabtu ʿunuqa khādimihā
sentences.l: And-by-God the-Mighty, were-it-not that-I fear (the) doing-ill (of) the-courtesy in (the) right (of) my-father Qamar al-Zamān and-my-brother the-king al-Asʿad, I-would-surely-go-in upon-her and-surely-strike her-neck as I-struck (the) neck (of) her-servant!
sentences.i: By God the Almighty, were it not that I fear to fail in the respect I owe my father Qamar al-Zamān and my brother King al-Asʿad, I would go in to her and strike off her head as I struck off her eunuch's!
sentences.n: “Her” here is Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, the stepmother, wife of his father and mother of his brother al-Asʿad: that is why he holds back. lawlā annī, “were it not that I”; the shadda of انّي is printed. isāʾat al-adab, “the spoiling of good manners”: isāʾa, Form IV verbal noun of s-w-ʾ, with the ء printed; adab, courtesy, the respect owed. fī ḥaqqi, “in the right of”, towards. The answer to lawlā takes the form of an oath's answer, la- with the energetic imperfect: la-adkhulanna, wa-aḍribanna, “I would surely enter … and surely strike”; Classical would more often say la-dakhaltu. The print has no shadda on these, and the energetic -anna is supplied here. The damma of ضربتُ is printed. ḍaraba ʿunuqahu, “to strike someone's neck”, to behead.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ خَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِ أُمِّهِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ وَهُوَ فِي غَايَةِ الْغَيْظِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu kharaja min ʿindi ummihi al-malikati Budūra wa-huwa fī ghāyati al-ghayẓi
sentences.l: Then he went-out from at his-mother, the-queen Budūr, and-he (was) in (the) utmost (of) the-rage.
sentences.i: Then he left his mother, Queen Budūr, in a towering rage.
sentences.n: min ʿindi, “from at”, from the presence of. Budūr is a diptote and takes a single fatḥa in the genitive. fī ghāyati al-ghayẓi, “in the utmost of rage”: ghāya, “the furthest point”, a stock way of saying “extremely”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ الْمَلِكَةَ حَيَاةَ النُّفُوسِ زَوْجَةَ أَبِيهِ مَا فَعَلَ بِخَادِمِهَا سَبَّتْهُ وَدَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَأَضْمَرَتْ لَهُ الْمَكْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā balagha al-malikata Ḥayāta al-Nufūsi zawjata abīhi mā faʿala bi-khādimihā sabbathu wa-daʿat ʿalayhi wa-aḍmarat lahu al-makra
sentences.l: And-when reached the-queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, (the) wife (of) his-father, what he-did with-her-servant, she-reviled-him and-prayed against-him and-hid-within for-him the-guile.
sentences.i: And when word reached Queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, his father's wife, of what he had done to her eunuch, she cursed him, called down evil on him, and secretly plotted against him.
sentences.n: balagha, “to reach”, takes its object first and its subject last: what reached the queen was mā faʿala, “what he had done”. faʿala bi-, “to do to”: bi- marks the one it is done to. The shadda of سبّته is printed. daʿā ʿalā, “to pray against”, to curse, the opposite of daʿā li-, “to pray for”. aḍmara, Form IV, “to conceal (in the heart)”: aḍmarat lahu al-makra, she harboured a plot against him; lahu, “for him”, the one it is meant for.

sentences.t: فَبَاتَ الْمَلِكُ الْأَمْجَدُ فِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ ضَعِيفًا مِنَ الْغَيْظِ وَالْقَهْرِ وَالْفِكْرِ وَلَمْ يَلَذَّ لَهُ أَكْلٌ وَلَا شُرْبٌ وَلَا مَنَامٌ
sentences.tr: fa-bāta al-maliku al-Amjadu fī tilka al-laylati ḍaʿīfan mina al-ghayẓi wa-al-qahri wa-al-fikri wa-lam yaladhdha lahu aklun wa-lā shurbun wa-lā manāmun
sentences.l: And-passed-the-night the-king al-Amjad in that night weak from the-rage and-the-vexation and-the-brooding, and-not was-sweet to-him eating nor drinking nor sleep.
sentences.i: King al-Amjad spent that night sick with rage, vexation and brooding, and found no pleasure in food or drink or sleep.
sentences.n: bāta, “to spend the night”, takes a predicate like kāna: bāta … ḍaʿīfan, “he spent the night weak”. min of cause, “from”. qahr, “being overpowered”, and so the helpless anger of one who has been wronged. fikr, “thought”, here anxious brooding. lam yaladhdha lahu, “was not sweet to him”: ladhdha, doubled verb, “to be pleasant”; its shadda is printed. akl, shurb, manām, “eating, drinking, sleep”: the stock list of what a troubled hero cannot enjoy.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ خَرَجَ أَخُوهُ الْمَلِكُ الْأَسْعَدُ وَجَلَسَ فِي مَجْلِسِ أَبِيهِ الْمَلِكِ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu kharaja akhūhu al-maliku al-Asʿadu wa-jalasa fī majlisi abīhi al-maliki Qamari al-Zamāni li-yaḥkuma bayna al-nāsi
sentences.l: And-when became-morning the-morning, went-out his-brother the-king al-Asʿad and-sat in (the) sitting-place (of) his-father the-king Qamar al-Zamān to-judge between the-people.
sentences.i: When morning came, his brother King al-Asʿad went out and sat in the seat of their father, King Qamar al-Zamān, to judge among the people.
sentences.n: aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu, “the morning became morning”: a stock way of saying “when morning came”, verb and subject from the same root ṣ-b-ḥ. akhūhu, “his brother”: al-Amjad's, whose sleepless night has just been told; now it is al-Asʿad's turn to sit in judgement. li-yaḥkuma: li- of purpose with the subjunctive, “in order to judge”. ḥakama bayna, “to judge between”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْأَ صْبَحَتْ أُمُّهُ حَيَاةُ النُّفُوسِ ضَعِيفَةً بِسَبَبِ مَا سَمِعَتْهُ عَنِ الْمَلِكِ الْأَمْجَدِ مِنْ قَتْلِهِ لِلْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad aṣbaḥat ummuhu Ḥayātu al-Nufūsi ḍaʿīfatan bi-sababi mā samiʿathu ʿani al-maliki al-Amjadi min qatlihi li-al-khādimi
sentences.l: And-already had-become his-mother Ḥayāt al-Nufūs weak, by-reason-of what she-had-heard-it about the-king al-Amjad, of his-killing of-the-servant.
sentences.i: His mother, Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, had woken that morning sick with what she had heard of King al-Amjad: that he had killed the eunuch.
sentences.n: The print divides these words wrongly, وقدا صبحت, carrying the first letter of aṣbaḥat back onto qad. The spacing is kept as printed, and each piece is pointed as part of the word it belongs to: wa-qad aṣbaḥat, “and she had become”. The shadda of امّه is printed. aṣbaḥa with a predicate in the accusative, ḍaʿīfatan, means “to become”, and also “to be so in the morning”; both fit here. ḍaʿīf, “weak”, here “unwell”: her rage matches the rage that kept al-Amjad sleepless. bi-sababi, “by reason of”: bi- of cause with sabab, “cause”. mā samiʿathu, “what she had heard”: -hu goes back to mā. min qatlihi, “namely his killing”: min spells out what the mā was. li-al-khādimi: li- marks the object of the verbal noun qatl, “his killing of the eunuch”, the one who had carried her letter.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ الْأَسْعَدَ لَمَّا جَلَسَ لِلْحُكْمِ فِي ذٰلِكَ الْيَوْمِ حَكَمَ وَعَدَلَ وَوَلَّى وَعَزَلَ وَأَمَرَوَنَهَي وَأَعْطَى وَوَهَبَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika al-Asʿada lammā jalasa li-al-ḥukmi fī dhālika al-yawmi ḥakama wa-ʿadala wa-wallā wa-ʿazala wa-amara wa-nahā wa-aʿṭā wa-wahaba
sentences.l: Then the-king al-Asʿad, when he-sat for-the-judging on that day, judged and-was-just, and-appointed and-dismissed, and-commanded-and-forbade, and-gave and-bestowed.
sentences.i: When King al-Asʿad sat in judgement that day, he judged and dealt justly, appointed and dismissed, commanded and forbade, gave and bestowed.
sentences.n: These are the stock pairs that described al-Amjad's day in the night before, with a pair added at the head, ḥakama wa-ʿadala, “judged and was just”, and one change: where al-Amjad “gave and withheld” (aʿṭā wa-manaʿa), al-Asʿad “gave and bestowed” (aʿṭā wa-wahaba). The shadda of وولّى is printed. The print runs wa-amara wa-nahā together as one word, وامرونهي, and it is kept as set; it also spells nahā with a dotted ي in place of ى, pointed here as printed. thumma inna opens the next step of the story; lammā … ḥakama, “when … he judged”. li-al-ḥukmi: li- of purpose, “for judging”.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ جَالِسًا فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحُكْمِ إِلَى قُرْبِ الْعَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal jālisan fī majlisi al-ḥukmi ilā qurbi al-ʿaṣri
sentences.l: And-not he-ceased sitting in (the) sitting-place (of) the-judging until (the) nearness (of) the-afternoon.
sentences.i: And he went on sitting in the seat of judgement until close on the afternoon prayer.
sentences.n: The print has قوب, a misprint for قرب, corrected here. lam yazal, “he did not cease”, with an accusative participle, jālisan: “he kept on sitting”. ʿaṣr, “afternoon”, is the time of the afternoon prayer, the third of the day's five; ilā qurbi al-ʿaṣri, “until the nearness of the afternoon”, means until that time was close.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ بُدُورَ أُمَّ الْمَلِكِ الْأَمْجَدِ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَى عَجُوزٍ مِنَ الْعَجَائِزِ الْمَاكِرَاتِ وَأَظْهَرَتْهَا عَلَى مَا فِي قَلْبِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malikata Budūra umma al-maliki al-Amjadi arsalat ilā ʿajūzin mina al-ʿajāʾizi al-mākirāti wa-aẓharathā ʿalā mā fī qalbihā
sentences.l: Then the-queen Budūr, (the) mother (of) the-king al-Amjad, sent to an-old-woman of the-old-women the-crafty, and-made-her-acquainted with what (was) in her-heart.
sentences.i: Then Queen Budūr, the mother of King al-Amjad, sent for one of those crafty old women and let her into the secret of her heart.
sentences.n: Now Budūr in her turn makes her move toward her husband's other son: each queen loves the other's son. The shadda of امّ is printed, and so is the ئ of العجائز. umma is accusative, in apposition to al-malikata after inna. arsala ilā, “to send to”, here “to send for”. ʿajūz, “old woman”, plural ʿajāʾiz: the crafty old go-between is a fixture of the Nights. aẓhara X ʿalā Y, Form IV, “to acquaint X with Y, let X into Y”.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَتْ وَرَقَةً لِتَكْتُبَ فِيهَا مُرَاسَلَةً لِلْمَلِكِ الْأَسْعَدِ بْنِ زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْكُوَ إِلَيْهِ كَثْرَةَ مَحَبَّتِهَا لَهُ وَوَجْدَهَا بِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhat waraqatan li-taktuba fīhā murāsalatan li-al-maliki al-Asʿadi ibni zawjihā wa-tashkuwa ilayhi kathrata maḥabbatihā lahu wa-wajdahā bihi
sentences.l: And-she-took a-sheet to-write on-it a-missive to-the-king al-Asʿad, son (of) her-husband, and-to-complain to-him (of) (the) greatness (of) her-love for-him and-her-passion for-him.
sentences.i: She took a sheet of paper to write on it a letter to King al-Asʿad, her husband's son, and to complain to him of how greatly she loved him and how she burned for him.
sentences.n: li-taktuba … wa-tashkuwa: li- of purpose governs both verbs, which are subjunctive, “to write … and to complain”. murāsala, Form III verbal noun of r-s-l, “correspondence”, here simply “a letter”. li-al-maliki: li- marks the one written to. ibn is written without its alif, بن, as in the night before. shakā ilā, “to complain to”; what is complained of is the direct object, kathrata, “the greatness (of)”. maḥabbatihā lahu: li- marks the one loved. wajdahā bihi, “her passion for him”: bi- marks its object.

sentences.t: فَكَتَبَتْ لَهُ هٰذِهِ السَّجَعَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-katabat lahu hādhihi al-sajaʿāti
sentences.l: And-she-wrote to-him these rhymed-phrases:
sentences.i: So she wrote him these lines of rhymed prose:
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. Like Ḥayāt al-Nufūs's letter in the night before, this one is in rhymed prose, sajʿ, and the print marks off its clauses with stars. lahu: li- marks the one written to.

sentences.t: مِمَّنْ تَلِفَتْ وَجْدًا وَشَوْقًا * إِلَى أَحْسَنِ النَّاسِ خَلْقًا وَخُلْقًا * الْمُعْجَبِ بِجَمَالِهِ * التَّائِهِ بِدَلَالِهِ * الْمُعْرِضِ عَنْ طَالِبِ وِصَالِهِ * الزَّاهِدِ فِي الْقُرْبِ مِمَّنْ خَضَعَ وَدَلَّ * إِلَى مَنْ جَفَا وَمَلَّ *
sentences.tr: mimman talifat wajdan wa-shawqan * ilā aḥsani al-nāsi khalqan wa-khulqan * al-muʿjabi bi-jamālihi * al-tāʾihi bi-dalālihi * al-muʿriḍi ʿan ṭālibi wiṣālihi * al-zāhidi fī al-qurbi mimman khaḍaʿa wa-dalla * ilā man jafā wa-malla *
sentences.l: From-one-who has-perished (of) ardour and-LONGING, * to (the) fairest (of) the-people in-make and-in-NATURE, * the-one-vain of-his-BEAUTY, * the-one-proud in-his-COQUETRY, * the-one-turning-away from (the) seeker (of) UNION-WITH-HIM, * the-one-indifferent to the-nearness of-one-who submitted and-made-BOLD, * to one-who was-harsh and-grew-WEARY. *
sentences.i: From one who has perished of passion and longing * to the fairest of all people in form and in nature, * who delights in his own beauty, * who is proud in his coy disdain, * who turns from her that seeks his love, * who cares nothing to be near one who has bowed before him and made bold in love, * to him who has been harsh and grown weary. *
sentences.n: The rhyme words are in capitals in the literal line. As in the night before, the letter opens with its sender: min, “from”, fused here with man, “one who”, as mimman. The sender speaks of herself with masculine forms through much of the letter (man, khaḍaʿa, dalla, and al-ʿāshiq al-mukmad below), as lovers in Arabic poetry commonly do, though talifat is feminine. talifa, “to perish, be ruined”. wajdan wa-shawqan and khalqan wa-khulqan are accusatives of specification: “in respect of ardour”, “in respect of make”. The print points the two words that differ only in their first vowel: khalq (fatḥa printed), “outward form”, and khulq (ḍamma printed), “inner nature, character”, a stock jingle. al-muʿjab bi-, “vain of”: bi- marks what he admires. al-tāʾih, “straying, lost”, hence “haughty”; bi-dalālihi, “in his coquetry”: bi- of cause. dalāl is the coy, teasing disdain of a beloved who knows he is loved. These genitives stand in apposition to aḥsani al-nāsi, “the fairest of people”. zāhid fī, “indifferent to”. dalla, of a lover, “to make bold, presume on being loved”, from the same root as dalāl; the shadda of دلّ and of ملّ is printed. Beside khaḍaʿa, “submitted”, one might expect ذلّ, dhalla, “was abased”, a single dot away; the print has دلّ, which makes sense as it stands and is kept. The second ilā, “to”, restates the addressee. The rhymes: shawqan / khulqan; jamālihi / dalālihi / wiṣālihi; dalla / malla. The ئ of التائه is printed.

sentences.t: مِنَ الْعَاشِقِ الْمُكْمَدِ * إِلَى الْمَلِكِ الْأَسْعَدِ * صَاحِبِ الْحُسْنِ الْفَائِقِ * وَالْجَمَالِ الرَّائِقِ * وَالْوَجْهِ الْأَقْمَرِ * وَالْجَبِينِ الْأَزْهَرِ * وَالضِّيَاءِ الْأَبْهَرِ *
sentences.tr: mina al-ʿāshiqi al-mukmadi * ilā al-maliki al-Asʿadi * ṣāḥibi al-ḥusni al-fāʾiqi * wa-al-jamāli al-rāʾiqi * wa-al-wajhi al-aqmari * wa-al-jabīni al-azhari * wa-al-ḍiyāʾi al-abhari *
sentences.l: From the-lover the-GRIEF-STRICKEN * to the-king al-ASʿAD, * (the) possessor (of) the-loveliness the-SURPASSING, * and-the-beauty the-CLEAR, * and-the-face the-MOON-BRIGHT, * and-the-brow the-SHINING, * and-the-radiance the-DAZZLING. *
sentences.i: From the grief-stricken lover * to King al-Asʿad, * lord of surpassing loveliness * and pure beauty, * of the moon-bright face, * the shining brow * and the dazzling radiance. *
sentences.n: The address is made a second time, now naming both parties: the sender as al-ʿāshiq, “the lover”, in the masculine, and the receiver by name, al-Asʿad, which rhymes with al-mukmad. mukmad, Form IV passive participle of k-m-d, “made sick with grief”. ṣāḥib, “companion, possessor”: ṣāḥibi al-ḥusni, “the possessor of loveliness”, simply “the lovely one”. The ئ of الفائق and of الرائق is printed. rāʾiq, “clear, pure”, of water or wine, and so of beauty. aqmar, “moon-bright” (from qamar, “moon”), azhar, “shining”, and abhar, “most dazzling”, are three adjectives of the pattern afʿal, and they make the third rhyme. The rhymes: al-mukmad / al-Asʿad; al-fāʾiq / al-rāʾiq; al-aqmar / al-azhar / al-abhar.

sentences.t: هٰذَا كِتَابِي إِلَى مَنْ حُبُّهُ أَذَابَ جِسْمِي * وَفَرَّقَ جِلْدِى وَعَظْمِى *
sentences.tr: hādhā kitābī ilā man ḥubbuhu adhāba jismī * wa-farraqa jildī wa-ʿaẓmī *
sentences.l: This (is) my-letter to one-whom his-love has-melted my-BODY * and-has-parted my-skin and-my-BONE. *
sentences.i: This is my letter to the one whose love has melted my body away * and parted my skin from my bones. *
sentences.n: kitāb, “a writing”, here “letter”. man ḥubbuhu, “one whom love of him …”: -hu is the beloved, and ḥubb is the love felt for him. The ḍamma and shadda of حُبّه are printed, and the shadda of فرّق. adhāba, Form IV of dh-w-b, “to melt”: love has wasted the body. farraqa, Form II, “to separate”: she is so wasted that skin and bone have parted company. The print spells jildī and ʿaẓmī with ى, جلدى وعظمى, as it often does for final ي. The rhyme: jismī / ʿaẓmī.

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ أَنَّنِي قَدْ عِيلَ صَبْرِى * وَتَحَيَّرْتُ فِي أَمْرِي * وَأَقْلَقَنِي الشَّوْقُ وَالسُّهَادُ * وَجَفَانِى الصَّبْرُ وَالرُّقَادُ * وَلَازَمَنِى الْحُزْنُ وَالسُّهَادُ * وَبَرَّحَ بِى الْوَجْدُ وَالْغَرَامُ * وَحُلُولُ الضَّنَى وَالسَّقَامِ *
sentences.tr: iʿlam annanī qad ʿīla ṣabrī * wa-taḥayyartu fī amrī * wa-aqlaqanī al-shawqu wa-al-suhādu * wa-jafānī al-ṣabru wa-al-ruqādu * wa-lāzamanī al-ḥuznu wa-al-suhādu * wa-barraḥa bī al-wajdu wa-al-gharāmu * wa-ḥulūlu al-ḍanā wa-al-saqāmi *
sentences.l: Know that-I — indeed has-been-exhausted my-PATIENCE, * and-I-have-become-bewildered in my-AFFAIR, * and-have-made-me-restless the-longing and-the-SLEEPLESSNESS, * and-have-shunned-me the-patience and-the-SLUMBER, * and-have-clung-to-me the-grief and-the-SLEEPLESSNESS, * and-have-tormented me the-ardour and-the-PASSION * and-(the)-alighting (of) the-wasting and-the-SICKNESS. *
sentences.i: Know that my patience is spent * and I am at a loss what to do; * longing and wakefulness give me no rest, * patience and sleep have forsaken me, * grief and wakefulness never leave me, * and ardour and passion torment me, * with wasting and sickness settled upon me. *
sentences.n: iʿlam, “know”, the imperative that often opens the body of a letter; its alif is only a helping vowel, so it takes no hamza. annanī qad ʿīla ṣabrī, “that I, my patience has run out”: the noun of anna is “I”, and the clause after it says what has befallen me. ʿīla, passive of ʿāla, “to overwhelm”: ʿīla ṣabrī, “my patience is at an end”. The print spells ṣabrī with ى here, as it does jafānī, lāzamanī and bī below, but amrī with ي. The shadda of تحيّرت is printed. taḥayyara fī amrihi, Form V, “to be at a loss in one's affair”. aqlaqa, Form IV, “to make restless”. al-suhād, “sleeplessness”, ends two clauses, the second time with its ḍamma printed, السُهاد: the rhyme simply repeats the word, with al-ruqād between. jafā, “to shun”, is the verb she used of him above; and ṣabr, “patience”, is lost a second time. lāzama, Form III, “to cling to, never leave”. barraḥa bi-, Form II, “to torment, distress sorely”: bi- marks the one tormented. ḥulūl, “alighting, settling (upon someone)”, is a third subject of barraḥa, beside al-wajdu and al-gharāmu. ḍanā, “wasting sickness”; saqām, “illness”. The rhymes: ṣabrī / amrī; al-suhād / al-ruqād / al-suhād; al-gharām / al-saqām.

sentences.t: فَالرُّوحُ تَفْدِيكَ * وَإِنْ كَانَ قَتْلُ الصَّبِّ يُرْضِيكَ * وَاللَّهُ يُبْقِيكَ * وَمِنْ كُلِّ سُوءٍ يَقِيكَ *
sentences.tr: fa-al-rūḥu tafdīka * wa-in kāna qatlu al-ṣabbi yurḍīka * wa-Allāhu yubqīka * wa-min kulli sūʾin yaqīka *
sentences.l: So-the-soul ransoms-YOU, * even-if is (the) killing (of) the-lovesick pleasing-YOU; * and-God preserves-YOU, * and-from every evil guards-YOU. *
sentences.i: My soul is your ransom, * even if the lover's death should please you. * May God preserve you * and keep you from every harm. *
sentences.n: The print has برضيك, a misprint for يرضيك, corrected here. al-rūḥu tafdīka, “the soul ransoms you”, that is, “my life for yours”, a common formula of devotion; rūḥ is treated as feminine. wa-in kāna, “even if it be”. ṣabb, “one in love, lovesick”, is her name for herself. Allāhu yubqīka and yaqīka are imperfects with the force of a prayer: “may God keep you alive”, “may He guard you”. yubqī, Form IV of b-q-y, “to make last”; waqā, yaqī, “to protect”, with min of what one is protected from. All four clauses rhyme in -īka, and the rhymed prose ends here.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ تِلْكَ السَّجَعَاتِ كَتَبَتْ هٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda tilka al-sajaʿāti katabat hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then after those rhymed-phrases she-wrote these verses:
sentences.i: Then, after the rhymed prose, she wrote these verses:
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. abyāt, plural of bayt, “a line of verse”; hādhihi and tilka are feminine singular, as with any plural of things.

sentences.t:
حَكَمَ الزَّمَانُ بِاَنَّنِي لَكَ عَاشِقُ * يَا مَنْ مَحَاسِنُهُ كَبَدْرٍ يُشْرِقُ
حُزْتَ الْمَلَاحَةَ وَالْفَصَاحَةَ كُلَّهَا * وَعَلَيْكَ مِنْ دُونِ الْبَرِيَّةِ رَوْنَقُ
وَلَقَدْ رَضِيتُ بِاَنْ تَكُوْنَ مُعَذِّبِيْ * فَعَسَى عَلَيَّ بِنَظْرَةٍ تَتَصَدَّقُ
مَنْ مَاتَ فِيكَ صَبَابَةً فَلَهُ الْهَنَا * لَا خَيْرَ فِيمَنْ لَا يُحِبُّ وَيَعْشَقُ
sentences.tr:
ḥakama al-zamānu bi-annanī laka ʿāshiqu * yā man maḥāsinuhu ka-badrin yushriqu
ḥuzta al-malāḥata wa-al-faṣāḥata kullahā * wa-ʿalayka min dūni al-bariyyati rawnaqu
wa-la-qad raḍītu bi-an takūna muʿadhdhibī * fa-ʿasā ʿalayya bi-naẓratin tataṣaddaqu
man māta fīka ṣabābatan fa-lahu al-hanā * lā khayra fīman lā yuḥibbu wa-yaʿshaqu
sentences.l:
Time has-decreed that-I to-you (am) a-lover, * O one-whose beauties (are) like-a-full-moon rising.
You-have-gathered the-comeliness and-the-eloquence, all-of-it, * and-upon-you, apart-from the-creation, (is) a-splendour.
And-truly I-am-content with-that you-be my-tormentor, * so-perhaps upon-me with-a-glance you-will-bestow-alms.
Whoever dies in-you of-passion, then-for-him (is) the-bliss; * no good (is) in-one-who does-not love and-desire.
sentences.i:
Time has decreed that I should be your lover, * O you whose beauties shine like the rising full moon.
All grace and all eloquence are yours, * and on you alone of all creation lies a splendour.
I am content that you should be my tormentor; * perhaps you will bestow on me the charity of a glance.
Whoever dies of passion for you, his is the bliss: * there is no good in one who does not love and long.
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. The metre is kāmil, and the lines rhyme in -qu: ʿāshiqu, yushriqu, rawnaqu, tataṣaddaqu, yaʿshaqu; the first line rhymes within itself, as an opening line often does. ʿāshiqu at the end of the first half-line has no tanwīn, which the rhyme drops. The print writes bi-annanī and bi-an with a bare alif, بِاَنَّنِي, بِاَنْ, the hamza unwritten, and puts a sukūn on the long vowels of تَكُوْنَ and مُعَذِّبِيْ. ḥakama bi-, “to decree”: bi- marks what is decreed. laka, “to you”: li- marks the one loved. ka-badrin: ka-, “like”, a full moon. ḥuzta, “you have won, gathered”, from ḥāza. min dūni, “to the exclusion of”, so “you alone of all creation”. raḍītu bi-: the verb takes bi- for what one accepts. ʿasā here takes a bare imperfect without an: “perhaps you will …”. taṣaddaqa ʿalā … bi-, Form V, “to give someone something in alms”: bi- marks the gift, a glance. fīka, “in you”: fī of cause, “for you, on your account”. ṣabābatan, “of ardent love”: accusative of cause. al-hanā, “bliss”, is spelled without its final hamza. fīman = fī man, “in one who”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ كَتَبَتْ أَيْضًا هٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma katabat ayḍan hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then she-wrote also these verses:
sentences.i: Then she wrote these verses as well:
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. ayḍan, “also, again”.

sentences.t:
اِلَيْكَ اَسْعَدُ اَشْكُو مِنْ لَهِيبِ جَوًى * فَارْحَمْ مُتَيَّمَةً بِالشَّوْقِ تَلْتَهِبُ
اِلَى مَتَى وَاَيَادِي الْوَجْدِ تَلْعَبُ بِي * وَالْعِشْقُ وَالْفِكْرُ وَالتَّسْهِيدُ وَالنَّصَبُ
طَوْرًا بِبَحْرٍ وَطَوْرًا اَشْتَكِي لَهَبًا * فِي مُهْجَتِي اِنَّ ذَا يَا مُنْيَتِي عَجَبُ
يَالَائِمِي خَلِّ لَوْمِي وَالْتَمِسْ هَرَبًا * مِنَ الْهَوَى فَدُمُوعُ الْعَيْنِ تَنْسَكِبُ
كَمْ صِحْتُ وَجْدًا مِنَ الْهِجْرَانِ وَاحَرَبًا * فَلَمْ يُفِدْنِي بِذَاكَ الْوَيْلُ وَالْحَرَبُ
اَمْرَضْتَنِي بِصُدُودٍ لَسْتُ اَحْمِلُهُ * اَنْتَ الطَّبِيبُ فَاَسْعِفْنِي بِمَا يَجِبُ
يَا عَاذِلِي كُفَّ عَنْ عَذْلِي مُحَاذَرَةً * كَيْلَا يُصِيبُكَ مِنْ دَاءِ الْهَوَى عَطَبُ
sentences.tr:
ilayka Asʿadu ashkū min lahībi jawan * fa-irḥam mutayyamatan bi-al-shawqi taltahibu
ilā matā wa-ayādī al-wajdi talʿabu bī * wa-al-ʿishqu wa-al-fikru wa-al-tashīdu wa-al-naṣabu
ṭawran bi-baḥrin wa-ṭawran ashtakī lahaban * fī muhjatī inna dhā yā munyatī ʿajabu
yā lāʾimī khalli lawmī wa-iltamis haraban * mina al-hawā fa-dumūʿu al-ʿayni tansakibu
kam ṣiḥtu wajdan mina al-hijrāni wā-ḥaraban * fa-lam yufidnī bi-dhāka al-waylu wa-al-ḥarabu
amraḍtanī bi-ṣudūdin lastu aḥmiluhu * anta al-ṭabību fa-asʿifnī bi-mā yajibu
yā ʿādhilī kuffa ʿan ʿadhlī muḥādharatan * kay-lā yuṣībuka min dāʾi al-hawā ʿaṭabu
sentences.l:
To-you, Asʿad, I-complain of (the) blaze (of) a-consuming-passion; * so-have-mercy (on) an-enslaved-woman (who) with-the-longing is-aflame.
Until when — and-(the)-hands (of) the-ardour play with-me, * and-the-love and-the-brooding and-the-wakefulness and-the-toil?
At-a-time in-a-sea, and-at-a-time I-complain-of a-flame * in my-heart's-blood; indeed this, O my-desire, (is) a-wonder.
O my-blamer, leave my-blaming and-seek a-flight * from the-love; for-(the)-tears (of) the-eye pour-down.
How-often have-I-cried-out (in) ardour from the-desertion, “Alas-ruin!” * and-not availed-me by-that the-woe and-the-ruin.
You-have-made-me-sick with-an-aversion I-am-not bearing-it; * you (are) the-physician, so-succour-me with-what is-needful.
O my-reproacher, hold-off from my-reproaching, (out of) caution, * lest strike-you, from (the) sickness (of) the-love, a-ruin.
sentences.i:
To you, Asʿad, I make my complaint of passion's blaze: * have pity on a woman enslaved, burning with longing.
How long must the hands of ardour play with me, * and love, and brooding, and wakefulness, and weariness?
Now I am drowned in a sea, now I cry out at a flame * in my heart's blood: this, my heart's desire, is a wonder.
You who blame me, leave off your blaming and seek a way to flee * from love, for the tears of my eyes are pouring down.
How often have I cried out in my passion at your coldness, “Alas, ruin!” * Yet woe and ruin have availed me nothing.
You have made me sick with a coldness I cannot bear; * you are the physician, so give me the cure I need.
You who reproach me, hold back your reproaches and beware, * lest the sickness of love strike you with ruin too.
sentences.n: The verses are pointed in the print and copied as printed. The metre is basīṭ, and the lines rhyme in -bu: taltahibu, naṣabu, ʿajabu, tansakibu, ḥarabu, yajibu, ʿaṭabu. The print writes the hamza of ilayka, Asʿadu, ashkū and the like as a bare alif with its vowel, اِلَيْكَ, اَسْعَدُ, the hamza unwritten; the hamza of lāʾimī and dāʾi is printed. Asʿadu: the name, without its article, called upon without yā, as verse allows. jawan, “consuming passion, inner burning”. mutayyama, “a woman enslaved by love”, passive participle of Form II of t-y-m: here the speaker is plainly a woman. bi-al-shawqi: bi- of cause, “with longing”. ilā matā, “until when?”, that is “how long?”; the wa- introduces the state, “while the hands of ardour play with me”, and the four nouns of the second half-line are further subjects of talʿabu. laʿiba bi-, “to play with”: bi- marks the plaything. tashīd, Form II verbal noun, “keeping awake”. ṭawran … wa-ṭawran, “at one time … at another”; bi-baḥrin, “in a sea”: bi- of place, the sea of her tears. muhja, “heart's blood, life”. dhā, “this”, is short for hādhā. munya, “wish, object of desire”. The print runs yā lāʾimī together, يَالَائِمِي, and it is kept as set. The lāʾim, “blamer”, and the ʿādhil, “reproacher”, are stock figures of love poetry who tell the lover to give up. wā-ḥarabā, the cry of lament with wā: “alas, ruin!”; the print gives it tanwīn, وَاحَرَبًا. ṣudūd, “turning away, aversion”. asʿafa, Form IV, “to help, grant one's need”: bi-mā yajibu, “with what is needful”, bi- marking the help given. muḥādharatan, “as a precaution”: accusative of cause. kay-lā, “so that … not”. After it Classical Arabic wants the subjunctive, yuṣībaka; the print points yuṣībuka, indicative, and it is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ بُدُورَ ضَمَّخَتْ وَرَقَةَ الرِّسَالَةِ بِالْمِسْكِ الْأَذْفَرِ وَلَفَّتْهَا فِي جَدَائِلِ شَعْرِهَا وَهِيَ مِنَ الْحَرِيرِ الْعِرَاقِيِّ وَشَرَارِيبُهَا مِنْ قُضْبَانِ الزُّمُرُّدِ الْأَخْضَرِ مُرَصَّعَةٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malikata Budūra ḍammakhat waraqata al-risālati bi-al-miski al-adhfari wa-laffathā fī jadāʾili shaʿrihā wa-hiya mina al-ḥarīri al-ʿirāqiyyi wa-sharārībuhā min quḍbāni al-zumurrudi al-akhḍari muraṣṣaʿatun bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari
sentences.l: Then the-queen Budūr steeped (the) sheet (of) the-letter with-the-musk the-pungent, and-wrapped-it in (the) braids (of) her-hair, and-they (were) of the-silk the-Iraqi, and-their-tassels (were) of rods (of) the-emerald the-green, studded with-the-pearls and-the-jewels.
sentences.i: Then Queen Budūr steeped the sheet of her letter in pungent musk and wrapped it in the braids of her hair, which were bound with Iraqi silk, their tassels made of rods of green emerald studded with pearls and gems.
sentences.n: Now it is Budūr's turn: she writes to al-Asʿad, her husband's son by Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, as Ḥayāt al-Nufūs wrote to al-Amjad. The shaddas of ثمّ, ضمّخت, لفّتها and مرصّعة are printed, and so is the ئ of جدائل. ḍammakha, Form II, “to steep, smear (with perfume)”: the verb whose participle muḍammakha described Ḥayāt al-Nufūs's silk. bi-al-miski: bi- marks what it is steeped in. al-misk al-adhfar, “pungent musk”, the stock epithet of the finest musk. wa-hiya mina al-ḥarīri al-ʿirāqiyyi, “and they were of Iraqi silk”: hiya, a feminine singular, refers to the braids, a plural of things; the braids are evidently plaited or bound with silk. sharārīb, plural of shurrāba, “tassel”, a later word. muraṣṣaʿa, Form II participle, “inlaid, studded”, is read here as a second predicate of sharārībuhā, “their tassels … studded”; it could equally be read accusative, muraṣṣaʿatan, describing the whole. bi-al-durri: bi- marks what they are studded with. durr, “pearls”; jawhar, “gems, jewels”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَلَّمَتْهَا إِلَى الْعَجُوزِ وَأَمَرَتْهَا أَنْ تُعْطِيَهَا لِلْمَلِكِ الْأَسْعَدِ ابْنِ زَوْجِهَا الْمَلِكِ قَمَرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma sallamathā ilā al-ʿajūzi wa-amarathā an tuʿṭiyahā li-al-maliki al-Asʿadi ibni zawjihā al-maliki Qamari al-Zamāni
sentences.l: Then she-handed-it to the-old-woman, and-ordered-her that she-give-it to-the-king al-Asʿad, (the) son (of) her-husband the-king Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.i: Then she handed it to the old woman and ordered her to give it to King al-Asʿad, the son of her husband King Qamar al-Zamān.
sentences.n: The shadda of سلّمتها is printed. sallama ilā, Form II, “to hand over to”. al-ʿajūz, “the old woman”: Budūr's go-between. tuʿṭiyahā li-al-maliki: as in the night before, li- marks the receiver, where Classical would give aʿṭā two objects; an makes tuʿṭiya subjunctive. ibn keeps its alif here, ابن, though before the same words, “her husband”, the print wrote it without the alif a few lines above (al-Asʿadi bni zawjihā); the print is not consistent.

sentences.t: فَرَاحَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مِنْ أَجْلِ خَاطِرِهَا وَدَخَلَتْ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ الْأَسْعَدِ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا وَسَاعَتِهَا وَكَانَ فِي خَلْوَةٍ عِنْدَ دُخُولِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-rāḥati al-ʿajūzu min ajli khāṭirihā wa-dakhalat ʿalā al-maliki al-Asʿadi min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā wa-kāna fī khalwatin ʿinda dukhūlihā
sentences.l: And-went the-old-woman for (the) sake (of) her-wish, and-entered upon the-king al-Asʿad from her-time and-her-hour; and-he-was in seclusion at her-entering.
sentences.i: The old woman went off to do her mistress's pleasure and went in to King al-Asʿad that very hour; he was alone when she entered.
sentences.n: min ajli khāṭirihā, “for the sake of her wish”: khāṭir, “mind, inclination”, and -hā is Budūr, whose wish the old woman goes to carry out. dakhala ʿalā, “to go in to (someone)”: the verb takes ʿalā for the person visited. min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā, “from her time and her hour”: at once, without delay, a stock phrase of the later language. khalwa, “privacy, being alone”.

sentences.t: فَنَاوَلَتْهُ الْوَرَقَةَ بِمَا فِيهَا وَقَدْ وَقَفَتْ سَاعَةً زَمَانِيَّةً تَنْتَظِرُ رَدَّ الْجَوَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-nāwalathu al-waraqata bi-mā fīhā wa-qad waqafat sāʿatan zamāniyyatan tantaẓiru radda al-jawābi
sentences.l: And-she-handed-him the-sheet with-what (was) in-it, and-she-stood an-hour of-time, waiting-for (the) return (of) the-answer.
sentences.i: She handed him the letter with all that was wrapped about it, and stood a while waiting for his reply.
sentences.n: nāwala, Form III, “to hand (something) to (someone)”, with two objects. bi-mā fīhā, “with what was in it”: bi- of accompaniment; the braids and their tassels go with the letter. sāʿatan zamāniyyatan, “an hour of time”: a stock phrase of the Nights for “a little while”, not a clock hour. tantaẓiru, Form VIII, “waiting”: an imperfect describing how she stood. radd al-jawāb, “the returning of the answer”, a reply; the shadda of ردّ is printed.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ قَرَأَ الْمَلِكُ الْأَسْعَدُ الْوَرَقَةَ وَفَهِمَ مَا فِيهَا ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ لَفَّ الْوَرَقَةَ فِى الْجَدَائِلِ وَوَضَعَهَا فِي جَيْبِهِ وَغَضِبَ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا مَا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ وَلَعَنَ النِّسَاءَ الْخَائِنَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qaraʾa al-maliku al-Asʿadu al-waraqata wa-fahima mā fīhā thumma baʿda dhālika laffa al-waraqata fī al-jadāʾili wa-waḍaʿahā fī jaybihi wa-ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan mā ʿalayhi min mazīdin wa-laʿana al-nisāʾa al-khāʾināti
sentences.l: And-at that read the-king al-Asʿad the-sheet and-understood what (was) in-it; then after that he-wrapped the-sheet in the-braids, and-put-it in his-pocket, and-grew-angry an-anger severe, not upon-it of increase, and-cursed the-women the-treacherous.
sentences.i: At that King al-Asʿad read the letter and understood what was in it. Then he wrapped it again in the braids and put it in the breast of his robe, and fell into a rage than which there could be none greater, and cursed all treacherous women.
sentences.n: The ء of قرأ and the ئ of الخائنات are printed, as is the shadda of لفّ. The print spells fī with ى once here, فى, and with ي just after. jayb, “the opening at the breast of a garment”, where things are carried: a pocket. ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan, “he was angered with a severe anger”: the verb's own verbal noun as its object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), for emphasis. mā ʿalayhi min mazīdin, “there is no increase upon it”: nothing could go beyond it, a stock intensifier. khāʾināt, “treacherous”, feminine plural of khāʾin.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ نَهَضَ وَسَحَبَ السَّيْفَ مِنْ غِمْدِهِ وَضَرَبَ رَقَبَةَ الْعَجُوزِ فَعَزَلَ رَأْسَهَا عَنْ جُثَّتِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu nahaḍa wa-saḥaba al-sayfa min ghimdihi wa-ḍaraba raqabata al-ʿajūzi fa-ʿazala raʾsahā ʿan juththatihā
sentences.l: Then he rose, and-drew the-sword from its-scabbard, and-struck (the) neck (of) the-old-woman, and-severed her-head from her-body.
sentences.i: Then he rose, drew his sword from its scabbard and struck the old woman on the neck, parting her head from her body.
sentences.n: The print has غمدة, a misprint for غمده, corrected here. thumma innahu, “then indeed he”: the usual narrative connective. saḥaba, “to drag, draw out”. ʿazala … ʿan, “to set apart from”, here “to sever from”. The ء of رأسها is printed. juththa, “body”, often “corpse”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ قَامَ وَتَمَشَّى حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى أُمِّهِ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ فَوَجَدَهَا رَاقِدَةً فِى الْفَرْشِ ضَعِيفَةً بِسَبَبِ مَا جَرَي لَهَا مِنَ الْمَلِكِ الْأَمْجَدِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika qāma wa-tamashshā ḥattā dakhala ʿalā ummihi Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi fa-wajadahā rāqidatan fī al-farshi ḍaʿīfatan bi-sababi mā jarā lahā mina al-maliki al-Amjadi
sentences.l: And-after that he-rose and-walked until he-entered upon his-mother Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and-found-her lying in the-bedding, weak, by-cause (of) what happened to-her from the-king al-Amjad.
sentences.i: After that he rose and walked until he came in to his mother, Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and found her lying in bed, weak from what had befallen her at King al-Amjad's hands.
sentences.n: The shadda of امّه is printed. tamashshā, Form V, “to walk along”. wajadahā rāqidatan … ḍaʿīfatan: two accusatives describing how he found her. farsh, “bedding, furnishings”: she is lying in her bed. bi-sababi, “by reason of”: bi- of cause. jarā, “to happen”, is printed with a dotted yāʾ, جري, here and once below, and is read jarā. lahā: li- marks the one it befell; min marks the one it came from. What befell her is al-Amjad's answer to her letter, told earlier in the night.

sentences.t: فَشَتَمَهَا الْمَلِكُ الْأَسْعَدُ وَلَعَنَهَا ثُمَّ خَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-shatamahā al-maliku al-Asʿadu wa-laʿanahā thumma kharaja min ʿindihā
sentences.l: And-reviled-her the-king al-Asʿad and-cursed-her, then he-went-out from with-her.
sentences.i: King al-Asʿad reviled her and cursed her, then went out and left her.
sentences.n: shatama, “to revile, abuse”. min ʿindihā, “from beside her”: ʿinda with min is the usual way to say “from someone's presence”.

sentences.t: فَاجْتَمَعَ بِأَخِيهِ الْمَلِكِ الْأَمْجَدِ وَحَكَي لَهُ جَمِيعَ مَا جَرَي لَهُ مَعَ أُمِّهِ الْمَلِكَةِ بُدُورَ وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِأَنَّهُ قَتَلَ الْعَجُوزَ الَّتِي جَاءَتْ لَهُ بِالرِّسَالَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ijtamaʿa bi-akhīhi al-maliki al-Amjadi wa-ḥakā lahu jamīʿa mā jarā lahu maʿa ummihi al-malikati Budūra wa-akhbarahu bi-annahu qatala al-ʿajūza allatī jāʾat lahu bi-al-risālati
sentences.l: And-he-met with-his-brother the-king al-Amjad, and-related to-him all what happened to-him with his-mother the-queen Budūr, and-informed-him of-that-he had-killed the-old-woman who came to-him with-the-letter.
sentences.i: Then he went to his brother King al-Amjad and told him all that had passed between him and al-Amjad's mother, Queen Budūr, and told him too that he had killed the old woman who brought him the letter.
sentences.n: ijtamaʿa bi-, Form VIII, “to meet with”: the verb takes bi- for the person met. ḥakā, “to relate”, is printed with ي, حكي, and read ḥakā. Of the two lahu, the first is al-Amjad, the one told, and the second al-Asʿad, the one it befell. ummihi, “his mother”, is al-Amjad's mother, Budūr; the shadda is printed. akhbarahu bi-annahu, “informed him that”: the verb takes bi- for what is told. jāʾat lahu bi-al-risālati, “came to him with the letter”: jāʾa bi- is “to bring”, the verb choosing bi-; the ء of جاءت is printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ يَا أَخِي لَوْلَا حَيَائِي مِنْكَ لَكُنْتُ دَخَلْتُ فِي هٰذِهِ السَّاعَةِ إِلَيْهَا وَقَطَعْتُ رَأْسَهَا مِنْ بَيْنِ كَتِفَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu wa-Allāhi yā akhī lawlā ḥayāʾī minka la-kuntu dakhaltu fī hādhihi al-sāʿati ilayhā wa-qaṭaʿtu raʾsahā min bayni katifayhā
sentences.l: Then he-said to-him: By-God, O my-brother, were-it-not-for my-shame from-you, I-would-have entered in this hour to-her, and-cut-off her-head from between her-two-shoulders.
sentences.i: Then he said to him: By God, my brother, were it not for the respect I owe you, I would have gone in to her this very hour and cut her head from between her shoulders.
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. ilayhā, “to her”, is Budūr: al-Asʿad holds back only because she is his brother's mother. ḥayāʾ, “shame, modesty”, here the deference that holds him back before al-Amjad; its ئ is printed, as is the ء of رأسها. lawlā, “were it not for”, takes a noun, and its answer takes la-: la-kuntu dakhaltu, “I would have gone in”, kāna with a perfect for a past that never happened. katifayhā, “her two shoulders”: dual, its nūn dropped before the suffix.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخُوهُ الْمَلِكُ الْأَمْجَدُ وَاللَّهِ يَا أَخِي إِنَّهُ قَدْ جَرَى لِي بِالْأَمْسِ لَمَّا جَلَسْتُ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ الْمَمْلَكَةِ مِثْلُ مَا جَرَى لَكَ فِى هٰذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhūhu al-maliku al-Amjadu wa-Allāhi yā akhī innahu qad jarā lī bi-al-amsi lammā jalastu ʿalā kursiyyi al-mamlakati mithlu mā jarā laka fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: And-said to-him his-brother the-king al-Amjad: By-God, O my-brother, indeed-it has happened to-me yesterday, when I-sat upon (the) throne (of) the-kingdom, (the) like (of) what happened to-you on this day.
sentences.i: His brother King al-Amjad said to him: By God, my brother, yesterday, when I sat on the throne of the kingdom, the very same thing happened to me as has happened to you today.
sentences.n: innahu, “indeed it”: -hu is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), pointing ahead to the whole statement; the real subject of jarā is mithlu mā, “the like of what”, held back to the end. This time jarā is spelled with ى, جرى. lī, laka: li- marks the one it befell. bi-al-amsi, “yesterday”: bi- of time. kursī al-mamlaka, “the chair of the kingdom”, the throne; the shadda of كرسيّ is printed.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ أُمَّكَ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيَّ رِسَالَةً بِمِثْلِ مَضْمُونِ هٰذَا الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna ummaka arsalat ilayya risālatan bi-mithli maḍmūni hādhā al-kalāmi
sentences.l: For your-mother sent to-me a-letter with-(the)-like (of the) content (of) this speech.
sentences.i: For your mother sent me a letter in just the same terms.
sentences.n: fa-inna, “for indeed”: fa- introduces the explanation. ummaka, “your mother”, is Ḥayāt al-Nufūs. The shaddas of امّك and اليّ are printed. bi-mithli, “with the like of”: bi- marks what the letter carried. maḍmūn, “content, purport”, a passive participle, “what is contained”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْبَرَهُ بِجَمِيعِ مَاجَرَى لَهُ مَعَ أُمِّهِ الْمَلِكَةِ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ يَاأَخِي لَوْلَا حَيَائِي مِنْكَ لَدَخَلْتُ إِلَيْهَا وَفَعَلْتُ بِهَا مِثْلَ مَا فَعَلْتُ بِالْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhbarahu bi-jamīʿi mā jarā lahu maʿa ummihi al-malikati Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi wa-qāla lahu wa-Allāhi yā akhī lawlā ḥayāʾī minka la-dakhaltu ilayhā wa-faʿaltu bihā mithla mā faʿaltu bi-al-khādimi
sentences.l: Then he-informed-him of-all what-happened to-him with his-mother the-queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and-said to-him: By-God, O-my-brother, were-it-not-for my-shame from-you, I-would-have-entered to-her and-done to-her (the) like (of) what I-did to-the-servant.
sentences.i: Then he told him all that had passed between him and al-Asʿad's mother, Queen Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and said to him: By God, my brother, were it not for the respect I owe you, I would have gone in to her and done to her what I did to the eunuch.
sentences.n: The print runs mā jarā and yā akhī together, ماجرى and يااخي; both are kept as set. akhbarahu bi-, “told him of”: the verb takes bi- for what is told. ummihi is now al-Asʿad's mother, Ḥayāt al-Nufūs; this time the print has no shadda on امه. la-dakhaltu: the answer to lawlā with la- and a plain perfect, beside la-kuntu dakhaltu a moment ago. The damma of فعلتُ, printed both times, marks the first person, “I did”. faʿala bi-, “to do (something) to”: the verb takes bi- for the one it is done to. al-khādim is the eunuch who brought Ḥayāt al-Nufūs's letter, whom al-Amjad killed earlier in the night.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا بَاتَا يَتَحَدَّثَانِ بَقِيَّةَ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ وَيَلْعَنَانِ النِّسَاءَ الْخَائِنَاتِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā bātā yataḥaddathāni baqiyyata tilka al-laylati wa-yalʿanāni al-nisāʾa al-khāʾināti
sentences.l: Then they-two spent-the-night talking-together (the) rest (of) that night and-cursing the-women the-treacherous.
sentences.i: Then the two of them spent the rest of that night talking together and cursing treacherous women.
sentences.n: bāta, “to spend the night”, here with an imperfect, “spent the night doing”: like kāna, it takes a verb describing the state. yataḥaddathāni, Form V dual, “the two talk together”; its shadda is printed, as is the ئ of الخائنات. baqiyyata, accusative of time, “for the rest of”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَاصَيَا بِكِتْمَانِ هٰذَا الْأَمْرِ لِئَلَّا يَسْمَعَ بِهِ أَبُوهُمَا الْمَلِكُ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ فَيَقْتُلَ الْمَرْأَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma tawāṣayā bi-kitmāni hādhā al-amri li-allā yasmaʿa bihi abūhumā al-maliku Qamaru al-Zamāni fa-yaqtula al-marʾatayni
sentences.l: Then they-two-charged-each-other with-(the)-concealing (of) this matter, lest hear of-it their-father the-king Qamar al-Zamān and-kill the-two-women.
sentences.i: Then each charged the other to keep the matter hidden, lest their father King Qamar al-Zamān should hear of it and put the two women to death.
sentences.n: tawāṣā bi-, Form VI, “to charge one another with”: the verb takes bi- for what is enjoined. kitmān, “concealing”. li-allā, “so that not, lest”: li- of purpose with an + lā; its ئ is printed. samiʿa bi-, “to hear of”: bi- marks what is heard about. fa-yaqtula, subjunctive, still governed by li-allā: “and so kill”. The ء of المرأتين is printed; al-marʾatayni, “the two women”, is the dual of al-marʾa.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالَا فِي غَمٍّ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālā fī ghammin tilka al-laylata ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And-not they-two-ceased (to be) in grief that night until the-morning.
sentences.i: And they stayed in grief all that night until morning.
sentences.n: lam yazālā, “they did not cease”: with a negative, zāla means “to go on, remain”. ghamm, “grief, distress”. tilka al-laylata, accusative of time, “that night”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ أَقْبَلَ الْمَلِكُ بِجَيْشِهِ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ وَجَلَسَ سَاعَةً عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ الْمَمْلَكَةِ ثُمَّ طَلَعَ إِلَى قَصْرِهِ وَصَرَفَ الْأُمَرَاءَ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu aqbala al-maliku bi-jayshihi mina al-ṣaydi wa-jalasa sāʿatan ʿalā kursiyyi al-mamlakati thumma ṭalaʿa ilā qaṣrihi wa-ṣarafa al-umarāʾa ilā ḥāli sabīlihim
sentences.l: And-when the-morning dawned, came the-king with-his-army from the-hunt, and-sat an-hour upon (the) throne (of) the-kingdom; then he-went-up to his-palace and-dismissed the-emirs to (the) state (of) their-way.
sentences.i: When morning came, the king returned from the hunt with his army and sat a while on the throne of the kingdom; then he went up to his palace and sent the emirs about their business.
sentences.n: aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu, “the morning came to morning”: verb and subject from the same root, a stock phrase. bi-jayshihi, “with his army”: bi- of accompaniment. The shadda of كرسيّ is printed. ṭalaʿa, “to go up”. ilā ḥāli sabīlihim, “to the state of their way”: off about their own affairs, a stock phrase of the later language.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ وَدَخَلَ الْقَصْرَ فَوَجَدَ زَوْجَتَيْهِ رَاقِدَتَيْنِ عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ وَهُمَا فِي غَايَةِ الضَّعْفِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma wa-dakhala al-qaṣra fa-wajada zawjatayhi rāqidatayni ʿalā al-firāshi wa-humā fī ghāyati al-ḍaʿfi
sentences.l: And-he-rose and-entered the-palace, and-found his-two-wives lying on the-bed, and-they-two (were) in (the) utmost (of) the-weakness.
sentences.i: He rose and went into the palace, and found his two wives lying in bed, utterly weak.
sentences.n: zawjatayhi, “his two wives”: dual, its nūn dropped before the suffix. rāqidatayni, feminine dual, describes how he found them. wa-humā fī ghāyati al-ḍaʿfi, “while they were at the utmost of weakness”: a circumstantial clause with wa-; ghāya, “utmost limit”. firāsh, “bed”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ عَمِلَتَا لِوَلَدَيْهِمَا مَكِيدَةً وَاتَّفَقَتَا عَلَى تَضْيِيعِ أَرْوَاحِهِمَا لِأَنَّهُمَا قَدْ فَضَحَتَا أَنْفُسَهُمَا مَعَهُمَا وَقَدْ خَشِيَتَا أَنْ يَصِيرَتَا تَحْتَ زَلَّتِهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad ʿamilatā li-waladayhimā makīdatan wa-ittafaqatā ʿalā taḍyīʿi arwāḥihimā li-annahumā qad faḍaḥatā anfusahumā maʿahumā wa-qad khashiyatā an yaṣīratā taḥta zallatihimā
sentences.l: And-they-two-had made for-their-two-sons a-plot, and-agreed on (the) losing (of) their-souls, because-they-two had exposed themselves with-them, and-they-two-had-feared that they-become under their-slip.
sentences.i: For they had laid a plot against their two sons and agreed to do away with them, because they had disgraced themselves before them, and feared they would end up at the sons' mercy for their lapse.
sentences.n: wa-qad with the perfect, “had already”: the narrator steps back to explain. li-waladayhimā: li- marks those the plot is aimed at, “against their two sons”. The duals shift between the women and the sons and only the sense tells them apart: -humā in arwāḥihimā and maʿahumā is the sons, in anfusahumā the women. taḍyīʿ, Form II verbal noun, “causing to be lost”: doing away with. faḍaḥa, “to expose, disgrace”. zalla, “slip, lapse”: their own guilty lapse; its shadda is printed. yaṣīratā: the print has يصيرتا, which joins the masculine prefix ya- to the feminine dual ending -tā; the expected form is taṣīrā, “that they two (women) should become”. It is kept as printed and vocalised yaṣīratā by that sense, but it may be a compositor's slip, and the reading is uncertain. taḥta, “under”: subject to the sons, with their lapse hanging over them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُمَا الْمَلِكُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ قَالَ لَهُمَا مَا لَكُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhumā al-maliku ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati qāla lahumā mā lakumā
sentences.l: And-when saw-them-two the-king in that state, he-said to-them-two: What (is) to-you-two?
sentences.i: When the king saw them in that state, he said to them: What ails you both?
sentences.n: The آ of رآهما is printed. ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati, “upon that state”: ʿalā of condition. mā lakumā, “what is to you two?”: li- marks the one something is wrong with, “what is the matter with you?”

sentences.t: فَقَامَتَا إِلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَتَا يَدَيْهِ وَعَكَسَتَا عَلَيْهِ الْمَسْأَلَةَ وَقَالَتَا لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ وَلَدَيْكَ اللَّذَيْنِ قَدْ تَرَبَّيَا فِي نِعْمَتِكَ قَدْ خَانَاكَ فِي زَوْجَتَيْكَ وَأَرْكَبَاكَ الْعَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmatā ilayhi wa-qabbalatā yadayhi wa-ʿakasatā ʿalayhi al-masʾalata wa-qālatā lahu iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna waladayka alladhayni qad tarabbayā fī niʿmatika qad khānāka fī zawjatayka wa-arkabāka al-ʿāra
sentences.l: And-they-two-rose to-him and-kissed his-two-hands, and-turned-around upon-him the-matter, and-said to-him: Know, O king, that your-two-sons, the-two-who have been-reared in your-bounty, have betrayed-you in your-two-wives and-made-you-ride the-shame.
sentences.i: The two rose to him and kissed his hands, and turned the whole matter on its head, saying to him: Know, O king, that your two sons, who were raised in your bounty, have betrayed you with your wives and brought shame upon you.
sentences.n: The shaddas of قبّلتا and تربّيا and the ء of المسألة are printed. ʿakasa al-masʾala, “to reverse the matter”: they tell it the wrong way round, putting their own guilt on the sons; ʿalayhi, “upon him”, the one deceived. qālatā lahu, “the two said to him”: the speech is put in both their mouths at once. iʿlam, “know”: its alif is hamzat al-waṣl, unpronounced after lahu. alladhayni, masculine dual relative in the accusative, agreeing with waladayka. tarabbā, Form V, “to be brought up”; fī niʿmatika, “in your bounty”, in your favour and at your expense. khānāka fī zawjatayka, “betrayed you in your two wives”: fī marks the matter of the betrayal. arkabāka al-ʿāra, “made you ride the shame”: Form IV, causative, with two objects; to bring disgrace on someone.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ قَمَرُ الزَّمَانِ مِنْ نِسَائِهِ هٰذَا الْكَلَامَ صَارَ الضِّيَاءُ فِي وَجْهِهِ ظَلَامًا وَاغْتَاظَ غَيْظًا شَدِيدًا حَتَّى طَارَ عَقْلُهُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْغَيْظِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Qamaru al-Zamāni min nisāʾihi hādhā al-kalāma ṣāra al-ḍiyāʾu fī wajhihi ẓalāman wa-ightāẓa ghayẓan shadīdan ḥattā ṭāra ʿaqluhu min shiddati al-ghayẓi
sentences.l: And-when heard Qamar al-Zamān from his-women this speech, became the-light in his-face darkness, and-he-was-enraged a-rage severe, until flew his-mind from (the) severity (of) the-rage.
sentences.i: When Qamar al-Zamān heard these words from his wives, the light in his face turned to darkness, and he was seized with such fury that his reason flew from him.
sentences.n: nisāʾ, “women”, here his wives; its ئ is printed, as is the ء of الضياء. ṣāra al-ḍiyāʾu fī wajhihi ẓalāman, “the light in his face became darkness”: ṣāra, “to become”, takes its predicate in the accusative; a stock image of the Nights for sudden rage or dismay. ightāẓa, Form VIII of gh-y-ẓ, “to be enraged”, with the verbal noun ghayẓan, for emphasis. ṭāra ʿaqluhu, “his mind flew”: he lost his wits. min shiddati, “from the severity”: min of cause.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِنِسَائِهِ أَوْضِحَا لِي هٰذِهِ الْقَضِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-nisāʾihi awḍiḥā lī hādhihi al-qaḍiyyata
sentences.l: And-he-said to-his-women: Make-clear, you-two, to-me this case.
sentences.i: And he said to his wives: Make this matter plain to me.
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. The print has القيضة, a misprint for القضية, corrected here. awḍiḥā, Form IV imperative, dual: he speaks to the two wives, though he named them with the plural nisāʾ. qaḍiyya, “case, affair”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْمَلِكَةُ بُدُورُ اعْلَمْ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ أَنَّ وَلَدَكَ الْأَسْعَدَ بْنَ حَيَاةِ النُّفُوسِ لَهُ مُدَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ وَهُوَ يُرَاسِلُنِي وَيُكَاتِبُنِي وَيُرَاوِدُنِي عَلَى الزِّنَا وَأَنَا أَنْهَاهُ عَنْ ذٰلِكَ وَلَمْ يَنْتَهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-malikatu Budūru iʿlam yā malika al-zamāni anna waladaka al-Asʿada ibna Ḥayāti al-Nufūsi lahu muddatun mina al-ayyāmi wa-huwa yurāsilunī wa-yukātibunī wa-yurāwidunī ʿalā al-zinā wa-anā anhāhu ʿan dhālika wa-lam yantahi
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-queen Budūr: Know, O king (of) the-time, that your-son al-Asʿad, son (of) Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, to-him (is) a-space of the-days, and-he keeps-sending-to-me and-writing-to-me and-seeking-to-seduce-me to the-fornication, and-I forbid-him from that, and-not he-desisted.
sentences.i: Queen Budūr said to him: Know, O king of the age, that your son al-Asʿad, the son of Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, has for some days now been sending me messages and letters and pressing me to fornicate with him; I forbade him, but he would not stop.
sentences.n: The print has انهاة, a misprint for انهاه, corrected here. yā malika al-zamāni, “O king of the age”, the usual courtly address. ibn is again written without its alif, بن, between al-Asʿad and his mother's name. lahu muddatun mina al-ayyāmi wa-huwa …, “he has a space of days while he …”: the later language's way of saying “for some time now he has been …”. yurāsilu and yukātibu, both Form III, “to correspond with”, by messenger and by letter. rāwada ʿalā, Form III, “to try to seduce into”: the verb takes ʿalā for what he urges. anhāhu, “I forbid him”, from nahā, with ʿan for what is forbidden. lam yantahi, Form VIII of n-h-y, “he did not desist”: jussive, its final yāʾ dropped.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَافَرْتَ أَنْتَ هَجَمَ عَلَيَّ وَهُوَ سَكْرَانُ وَالسَّيْفُ فِي يَدِهِ مَسْلُولٌ فَضَرَبَ بِهِ خَادِمِي فَقَتَلَهُ وَرَكِبَ عَلَى صَدْرِي وَالسَّيْفُ فِي يَدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā sāfarta anta hajama ʿalayya wa-huwa sakrānu wa-al-sayfu fī yadihi maslūlun fa-ḍaraba bihi khādimī fa-qatalahu wa-rakiba ʿalā ṣadrī wa-al-sayfu fī yadihi
sentences.l: And-when you-travelled, you, he-burst upon-me, and-he (was) drunk, and-the-sword in his-hand drawn; and-he-struck with-it my-servant and-killed-him, and-mounted upon my-breast, and-the-sword in his-hand.
sentences.i: When you went away, he burst in on me drunk, his sword drawn in his hand; he struck my servant with it and killed him, and got on top of me, the sword still in his hand.
sentences.n: The print has يدة twice here, a misprint for يده, corrected here both times. The fatḥa of سافرتَ is printed, marking “you” (m.), and the pronoun anta repeats it for emphasis; the shadda of عليّ is printed. hajama ʿalā, “to burst in on, fall upon”. sakrān, “drunk”, takes no tanwīn. wa-al-sayfu fī yadihi maslūlun, “with the sword in his hand, drawn”: a circumstantial clause with wa-; maslūl, “unsheathed”. ḍaraba bihi, “struck with it”: bi- of the instrument. khādimī, “my servant”: in her version the old woman al-Asʿad killed becomes a servant cut down defending her. rakiba ʿalā ṣadrī, “mounted on my breast”: overpowered her.

sentences.t: فَخِفْتُ أَنْ يَقْتُلَنِي إِذَا مَانَعْتُهُ كَمَا قَتَلَ خَادِمِي فَقَضَى أَرَبَهُ مِنِّي غَصْبًا
sentences.tr: fa-khiftu an yaqtulanī idhā mānaʿtuhu kamā qatala khādimī fa-qaḍā arabahu minnī ghaṣban
sentences.l: And-I-feared that he-kill-me if I-resisted-him, as he-killed my-servant; and-he-accomplished his-need from-me by-force.
sentences.i: I feared he would kill me if I resisted him, as he had killed my servant; and he took his pleasure of me by force.
sentences.n: The damma of فخفتُ is printed, marking “I”: khiftu, from khāfa, the long vowel shortened before the ending. an yaqtulanī, subjunctive after an. mānaʿa, Form III, “to resist, hold off”. kamā, “just as”: ka-, “like”, + mā, “what”. qaḍā arabahu, “he accomplished his need”: he had his way with her; arab, “need, desire”. minnī, “from me”, its shadda printed. ghaṣban, “by force”: an accusative of manner.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ تُخَلِّصْ حَقِّي مِنْهُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ قَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي بِيَدِي وَلَيْسَ لِي حَاجَةٌ بِالْحَيَوٰةِ فِى الدُّنْيَا بَعْدَ هٰذَا الْفِعْلِ الْقَبِيحِ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam tukhalliṣ ḥaqqī minhu ayyuhā al-maliku qataltu nafsī bi-yadī wa-laysa lī ḥājatun bi-al-ḥayāti fī al-dunyā baʿda hādhā al-fiʿli al-qabīḥi
sentences.l: And-if not you-recover my-right from-him, O king, I-have-killed myself with-my-hand; and-not-is to-me a-need of-the-life in the-world after this deed the-foul.
sentences.i: And if you do not exact my due from him, O king, I will kill myself with my own hand, for I have no use for life in this world after so foul a deed.
sentences.n: in lam tukhalliṣ … qataltu, “if you do not recover … I have killed”: a perfect in the answer of a condition looks forward, “I will kill”. khallaṣa al-ḥaqqa min, Form II, “to recover one's right from”, to exact redress. bi-yadī, “with my hand”: bi- of the instrument. laysa lī ḥājatun bi-, “I have no need of”: ḥāja takes bi- for what is needed. al-ḥayāt is spelled الحيوة, with wāw, the old spelling of this word familiar from the Qurʾān; it is pointed with a dagger alif over the wāw. al-dunyā, “this world”. The print spells fī with ى here, فى.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ حَيَاةُ النُّفُوسِ وَهِيَ مَفْجُوعَةٌ بِالْبُكَا وَأَيْضًا بِمِثْلِ مَا أَخْبَرَتْهُ بِهِ ضَرَّتُهَا بُدُورُ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarathu Ḥayātu al-Nufūsi wa-hiya mafjūʿatun bi-al-bukā wa-ayḍan bi-mithli mā akhbarathu bihi ḍarratuhā Budūru
sentences.l: And-informed-him Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, and-she (was) stricken with-the-weeping, also, of-(the)-like (of) what informed-him of-it her-fellow-wife Budūr.
sentences.i: And Ḥayāt al-Nufūs, choking with tears, told him the very same tale that her fellow wife Budūr had told.
sentences.n: wa-hiya mafjūʿatun bi-al-bukā, “while she was stricken with weeping”: a circumstantial clause; mafjūʿ, “stricken, grief-struck”, and bi- marks what overcomes her. The print spells al-bukāʾ without its final hamza, البكا, as it does with many words in -āʾ. wa-ayḍan, “also”, stands oddly before what it qualifies: she too told him the like. akhbara bi-, “to tell of”: the verb takes bi- for the news, in bi-mithli and again in bihi, which goes back to mā. ḍarra, “fellow wife”, one of two wives of the same man; its shadda is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazād, and-she-fell-silent from the-permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech allowed her.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as at the end of every night. The rhyme falls on al-ṣabāḥ / al-mubāḥ.
